title: A smooth algebra over a normal ring is a normal ring
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings which is smooth in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] ($S$ finitely presented over $R$, $H_1(L_{S/R})=0$, $\Omega_{S/R}$ finite projective). If $R$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] (every localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ at a prime is a normal domain), then $S$ is a normal ring.

source.place: Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma Tag 033C (lemma-normal-goes-up, algebra.tex line 46563); its proof uses Lemma Tag 0C22 (lemma-normal-goes-up-noetherian, line 46541), Lemma Tag 033B (lemma-reduced-goes-up), the list of Section section-smooth-overview (flat with regular fibres; remark (10), descent of a smooth ring map to a finitely generated Z-subalgebra), Proposition ubiquity-nagata and Lemma Tag 037D (lemma-colimit-normal-ring, line 8312)

proof.text: *The Noetherian case.* Assume moreover that $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. A smooth ring map is of finite presentation, in particular of finite type [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], so $S$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]; $\varphi$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be a prime and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ its residue field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The fibre ring $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is smooth over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ by base change [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] (1); the field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a regular ring [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring], so $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a regular ring by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] ('flat with regular fibres', Section 00TZ), hence a normal ring by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal] ('in particular, the fibres are normal'). Thus $R\to S$ satisfies hypotheses (1)-(5) of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-normal-fibres-noetherian-normal] and $S$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring].

source.place: Lemma Tag 033C (lemma-normal-goes-up), proof, first paragraph, with Lemma Tag 0C22 (lemma-normal-goes-up-noetherian) and the list of Section Tag 00TZ (section-smooth-overview)

proof.text: *Reduction to $R$ a normal domain.* Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$; we must show that $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Since $R$ is normal, $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a normal domain. Put $S'=S\otimes_RR_{\mathfrak p}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] (1), $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S'$ is smooth, and by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] $S\to S'$ is the localization of $S$ at the multiplicative set $\varphi(R\setminus\mathfrak p)$, i.e. $S'=S_{\mathfrak p}$. This set does not meet $\mathfrak q$, so $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak qS'$ is a prime of $S'$ and $(S')_{\mathfrak q'}\cong S_{\mathfrak q}$ (a localization of a localization at a larger multiplicative set, [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]). Hence if the lemma holds for $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S'$, then $S'$ is a normal ring and $S_{\mathfrak q}\cong(S')_{\mathfrak q'}$ is a normal domain. So it suffices to prove the lemma when $R$ is a normal domain, which we assume from now on; let $K$ be its field of fractions. (Stacks first notes that $R$, hence $S$ by Lemma 033B, is reduced; that remark is not used in the argument and is omitted here.)

*A model over a finitely generated subring.* By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-algebra-finite-type-model] there are a subring $R_0\subseteq R$ generated by finitely many elements, a smooth ring map $R_0\to S_0$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $S\cong R\otimes_{R_0}S_0$. As a subring of the domain $R$, $R_0$ is a domain, and its field of fractions $K_0$ is a subfield of $K$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 033C, proof, third paragraph, first sentence: remark (10) of Section Tag 00TZ, i.e. Lemma Tag 00TP (lemma-finite-presentation-fs-Noetherian)

proof.text: *Normalizations of finitely generated subrings lie in $R$.* Let $A\subseteq R$ be a subring generated by finitely many elements; it is a domain with fraction field $K_A\subseteq K$. Let $A'\subseteq K_A$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $K_A$. (a) By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-algebraic-extension-normal] (with $P=A$ and the algebraic extension $L=K_A$ of $K_A$), $A'$ is a normal domain with fraction field $K_A$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. (b) $A'\subseteq R$: an $x\in A'$ is an element of $K$ which is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in $A\subseteq R$, and $R$ is a normal domain, i.e. integrally closed in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], so $x\in R$. (c) By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-z-domain-normalization-finite] $A'$ is a finitely generated $A$-module, so $A'$ is generated as a ring by the ring generators of $A$ together with finitely many module generators; hence $A'$ is of finite type over the Noetherian ring $\mathbf Z$ (a principal ideal domain) and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. (d) If $A\supseteq R_0$, then $A'\supseteq R_0'$ (an element of $K_0\subseteq K_A$ integral over $R_0$ is integral over $A$). Stacks: 'As $R_0$ is a Nagata domain its integral closure $R_0'$ is finite over $R_0$. Moreover, as $R$ is a normal domain it is clear that $R_0'\subset R$.'

source.place: Lemma Tag 033C, proof, third paragraph, with Proposition Tag 0335 (proposition-ubiquity-nagata)

proof.text: *$R$ is a directed union of normal Noetherian domains $A$, and each $S_A$ is normal.* Let $\Lambda$ be the set of subrings $A\subseteq R$ that contain $R_0$, are generated by finitely many elements and are normal domains, ordered by inclusion. By step 4, $R_0'\in\Lambda$, every $A\in\Lambda$ contains $R_0'$ (step 4 (d), as $A=A'$), and every $A\in\Lambda$ is a Noetherian normal domain. $\Lambda$ is directed: for $A_1,A_2\in\Lambda$ the subring $B$ generated by $A_1\cup A_2$ is finitely generated and contains $R_0$, and $B'\in\Lambda$ (step 4) contains $A_1$ and $A_2$. $\bigcup_{A\in\Lambda}A=R$: for $x\in R$ the normalization of the subring $R_0[x]$ lies in $\Lambda$ and contains $x$. For $A\in\Lambda$ put $S_A=A\otimes_{R_0}S_0$. Then $A\to S_A$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] (1); $A$ is a normal ring, since each localization $A_{\mathfrak p}$ of the normal domain $A$ is a normal domain [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]; and $A$ is Noetherian. By step 1, $S_A$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. (Stacks: 'we may replace $R_0$ by $R_0'$ ... and assume that $R_0$ is a normal Noetherian domain. By the first paragraph of the proof we conclude that $S_0$ is a normal ring.')

source.place: Lemma Tag 033C, proof, third paragraph ('In this way we see that $R=\bigcup R_\lambda$ is the union of normal Noetherian domains')

proof.text: *$S$ is the directed colimit of the rings $S_A$.* For $A\subseteq B$ in $\Lambda$ let $S_A\to S_B$ and $S_A\to R\otimes_{R_0}S_0$ be the ring maps induced by the inclusions ($a\otimes s\mapsto a\otimes s$). Put $M_0=S_{R_0'}=R_0'\otimes_{R_0}S_0$; by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change], $A\otimes_{R_0'}M_0\cong S_A$ for $A\in\Lambda$ and $R\otimes_{R_0'}M_0\cong R\otimes_{R_0}S_0$, compatibly with these maps. The directed union $R$ of the $A\in\Lambda$ is their colimit in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] (a compatible family of ring maps $A\to T$ defines one map on the union). Hence [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise], applied to the directed set $\Lambda$ with least element $R_0'$ and $M_0$, gives: (1) every element of $R\otimes_{R_0}S_0$ is the image of an element of some $S_A$; (2) an element of $S_A$ with image $0$ in $R\otimes_{R_0}S_0$ maps to $0$ in some $S_B$, $B\supseteq A$. From (1), (2) and directedness, $R\otimes_{R_0}S_0$ with the ring maps $S_A\to R\otimes_{R_0}S_0$ is the colimit of the directed system of rings $(S_A)_{A\in\Lambda}$: for a compatible family of ring maps $\nu_A:S_A\to T$, the map $u$ sending the image of $t\in S_A$ to $\nu_A(t)$ is well defined by (2), defined everywhere by (1), and additive and multiplicative because any two elements come from one $S_A$. Composing with the isomorphism $S\cong R\otimes_{R_0}S_0$ of step 3, $S=\varinjlim_{A\in\Lambda}S_A$ in commutative rings. (Stacks: '$S=\colim R_\lambda\otimes_{R_0}S_0$'.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 033C, proof, third paragraph, last two sentences; with Lemma Tag 00DD (lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* The nonempty directed set $\Lambda$ is a filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], each $S_A$ is a normal ring (step 5), and $S$ is their colimit in commutative rings (step 6). By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-normal-ring], $S$ is a normal ring. With step 2 this proves the lemma for every normal ring $R$.
